name: Cache timing history sniffing
plain: Times how fast a resource loads to guess whether the person already visited a site.
meaning: A cached image or script loads in milliseconds, an uncached one in tens. Probing resources from other sites, or the status of a login, reveals browsing history. Cache partitioning mostly ended the cross-site variant.

steps: Choose a resource unique to a target site

limits.headline: Can time how fast something loads to guess if you visited a site before
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Time how fast an image or script loads
Guess it was cached if it loads in a few milliseconds
Learn if you have visited some sites or are logged in
cannot: Work as well now that browsers keep separate caches per site
See what you did on the other site
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari now partition the cache per site, which breaks most of this.

story.what_it_is: A site times how fast something loads to guess if you have already visited another site.

marketing.name: HTTP cache partitioning
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes splitting the cache by site so one site cannot learn what you visited elsewhere.

story.for_you: You never see it. A page asks for a picture from another site and watches how quickly it appears. A fast load suggests you have been there before. Newer browsers have mostly blocked this.
story.for_makers: It once let a site learn your browsing history without asking. Browsers now keep a separate cache for each site. Researchers and security teams still test it, and old browsers can still be fooled.

use_cases.example: A researcher shows that a news page can tell if you visited a bank by timing a logo load.
An ad network guesses that you are in market for a car by checking which dealers' images are in cache.
A social site checks whether you have seen a rival site recently to tune what it shows.
A shop checks if you saw a competitor's product images to adjust a promo.
A web performance team uses cache timing in tests to see how much a page benefits from caching.
A paywall tests whether you came from a certain site by checking for its assets.
A security team reviews logs for pages that probe other sites' files.

technical_bounds: Partitioned caches make cross-site probing fail in all three major browsers

value.abuse: Browsing history leak, login state detection

history.change: Safari partitions HTTP cache by first party
HTTP cache partitioned by top-level site and frame site
